edit.description: `FieldPath.spelling` (36) is derived state stored beside `steps`, hand-maintained two different ways: `parse` (67) and `split_element` (155) build it from steps through `steps_to_spelling` (209), while `split_leaf` (119) cuts the stored string with `parent_spelling` (203). No production site reads it — `engine.rs` (300, 1742) and `extract.rs` (445) consume the returned paths' `locate` only, and the `#[allow(dead_code)] fn spelling` (83) has this module's own tests (419, 427, 450, 458, 466, 482) as its only callers. Drop the field, derive the spelling from `steps` through the one renderer, delete `parent_spelling`, and scope the accessor to the callers it actually has instead of silencing the compiler over it.

summary: A field path's author-facing spelling is computed from its steps, not stored beside them and maintained two ways for no production reader.

per.section: Derived state is computed, never stored beside its source

tests.asserts: every admissible spelling round-trips through the steps — `steps_to_spelling(steps_of(s)) == s` over a bare name, `owner.name`, `plugins[*]`, `plugins[*].source`, `matrix[*][*].id` and `disable-model-invocation` — which is what licenses removing the stored copy; the existing `split_leaf`/`split_element` spelling assertions stay green on the computed form.

acceptance: `cargo test` green with the round-trip pin, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean, and src/address.rs carrying one spelling derivation and no `#[allow(dead_code)]`.
notes: The field's doc calls it 'the form every diagnostic names' — untrue at HEAD: `refusal` and `empty_segment` take the author's raw `&str` at parse time, before a `FieldPath` exists. That prose rides this entry. The compiled `query` stays stored: a cached derivation with one immutable home, paid for per `locate` at tree scale. scoped at 06209dfe
